chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Nakha'i and from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

Regarding a man who performs Tawaf and then a need presents itself to him, he said: 'There is no harm in him going for his own need or the need of another, and interrupting the Tawaf; and if he wishes to rest and sit, there is no harm in that. When he returns, he builds upon his Tawaf. If it is a voluntary Tawaf, he builds upon the first two Shaws (paces/circles); and if it is a mandatory Tawaf, then he went out for a need with a man, he does not build, nor for his own need.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because he only said 'he does not build' meaning on the Shaw and the two Shaws, distinguishing between the Tawaf of the obligation and the Tawaf of the sunnah. Do you not see that he said at the beginning of the report 'there is no harm in that, when he returns he builds upon his Tawaf'? Then he introduced a ruling specific to the voluntary Tawaf, which is the permissibility of building upon less than half. Then he followed that with his saying 'and if it was in the Tawaf of obligation, he did not build', meaning what was permissible for him in the voluntary Tawaf, and this is not contradictory to what we presented. And whoever is in the Tawaf and the time for a mandatory Salat enters, let him interrupt the Tawaf and pray, then build upon it from where he interrupted. He narrated that.

key_terms.بِنَاء: Building/Resuming (continuing from the point of interruption)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for interrupting Tawaf for a need or prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from the Imams, clarifying the jurisprudential distinction between Nafilah (voluntary) and Fard (mandatory) Tawaf regarding interruption for needs or prayer. The text emphasizes that while voluntary circumambulation allows resumption from any point, mandatory Tawaf requires stricter continuity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual acts. This hadith also highlights the priority of Salah, mandating that if prayer time enters during Tawaf, the pilgrim must interrupt to pray and then resume, underscoring the balance between ritual devotion and obligatory duties.
